Quick infra read — high level notes / blockers / info required:

1) Control plane topology options
   - Private control plane inside customer VPC (preferred): requires bi-directional VPN or private peering and a small management endpoint in Helios account. No data egress required if control plane only carries orchestration metadata.
   - On-prem appliance: feasible for air-gapped sites but expect additional ops (on-site support + regular image updates).

2) Network & operations prerequisites
   - Need Helios IP ranges, NAT/egress rules, and list of firewall rules for kube control plane + metrics/trace endpoints. Recommended ports: 443 (control plane), 50051 (gRPC internal), ephemeral for KV cache; explicit list in separate doc.
   - BGP peering optional; VPN with clear routing is sufficient. If Helios wants private peering we’ll need ASN details and support windows for maintenance.

3) Security/hardware
   - KMS: support for external KMS via TLS + IP allowlisting. HSM integration (PKCS#11) for key wrap is possible but will add 2–3 engineer-weeks for validation.
   - Disk encryption and in-memory key handling validated but will require runtime config audit.

4) Pilot effort estimate (rough)
   - Architecture planning: 1.5 engineer-weeks (infra + networking)
   - Initial deployment + validation: 2.5 engineer-weeks (runtime + infra)
   - Security/compliance glue (inc. KMS/HSM validation): 1 engineer-week (security + infra)
   => total ~5 engineer-weeks to get a one-model pilot standing up (assumes Helios provides network contacts and IP ranges within 3 business days).

5) Constraints & tradeoffs
   - Autoscaling across private/environment boundary will be constrained; recommend conservative burst limits for first 3 months.
   - On-prem will require a modest runbook and remote-support VPN access; confirm whether Helios permits our engineering VPN access.

Action items for Helios (needed to hit Friday deliverable):
   - Confirm network contact + provide CIDR ranges and firewall owner.
   - Indicate preference: VPC-managed control plane vs fully air-gapped appliance.

I’m attaching a short checklist (I’ll share the checklist link on the drive) and will prepare a 1-page infra-readout for the Friday summary.

—Dylan

Security quick-take after scanning their questionnaire and the SOW:

- Evidence & gaps:
  - SOC2: Helios expects SOC2-aligned controls for the private deploy. We can provide mapping to our SOC2 controls for the hosted bits, but for a private control plane + on-prem the customer owns some controls (network, physical security). We should explicitly call out shared responsibilities in SOW.
  - Audit logs: Need confirmation of log collection endpoints and retention window; our default retention is 90 days unless specified.

- Remote support and access
  - If we require remote debug access to on-prem components, Helios must approve a secure jump host or temporary support VPN. Request they confirm acceptable support model.

- HSM/KMS
  - HSM integration will be scoped as professional services. If Helios expects on-site HSM provisioning we should price it separately.

- Compliance deliverables to include in SOW
  - Responsibility matrix (who owns what control)
  - Evidence list (SOC2 mapping, penetration test results, encryption descriptions)
  - Change-control process for runtime upgrades

I’ll prepare suggested SOW language and a prioritized list of questionnaire items to close. For now, we should ask procurement for an initial procurement timeline and whether Helios requires vendor security review forms beyond the spreadsheet attached.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
